card.name: Drug interaction wording and dose spacing
card.fires_on: Punctuation, linking words or partial words inside drug-interaction statements, such as the comma after "administered concurrently" or "hours" in "at least 2 hours before".

modes.label: Concurrent use phrasing
modes.description: A comma, "and" or "may" right after a phrase about concurrent use or raised levels of an interacting drug.
modes.example: When administered concurrently<<,>> the following drugs may interact with thiaz

modes.label: Hours before or after
modes.description: The word "hours" in spacing instructions for taking one drug before or after another.
modes.example: take these medications at least 2<< hours>> before and not less than 6 hours

modes.label: Inside drug or condition names
modes.description: A middle piece of a drug or muscle-injury term in an interaction table or warning.
modes.example: The risk of myopathy and rhab<<d>>omyolysis is increased with concom

card.plain: It marks spots in drug-interaction text where the next words will describe what happens with another drug or how to space doses.
